title: Converge async and realtime streams into single canonical per-model meter with retention-aware smoothing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Console per-model charts show transient spikes and attribution flicker when late/backfilled async enrichment events merge with low-latency streaming ingest. This leads to customer confusion, incorrect quota burn visuals, and support tickets. Goal: produce a single, deterministic per-model "canonical meter" that reconciles realtime streaming events and delayed backfills without double-counting, provides explainability in the Console, and supports efficient retroactive corrections for long-tail late events.

Scope:
- Define canonical windowing semantics and idempotency rules for events coming from realtime stream vs async enrichment/backfill pipelines.
- Implement event-weighting and retention-aware smoothing on the metrics ingestion layer so that late events update totals but do not create discontinuous spikes in per-model charts.
- Add reconciliation job that computes and emits finalized per-hour per-model deltas after a 48-hour stabilization window.
- Surface "as-of" vs "finalized" views in Console for customers to understand how recent backfills may affect charts.
- Add deterministic deduplication using persistent idempotency keys for events that transit both pipelines.

Success criteria:
- Eliminate double-counts from cross-pipeline delivery (target <0.1% residual divergence after reconciliation).
- Reduce customer-facing per-model visual anomalies (spike frequency) by >90% in a 14-day A/B run.
- Provide audit trail links from Console chart points to reconciliation job runs and original event IDs.
comments: 2026-01-12 @Aisha Patel: Initial triage; reproducer dashboards created in Grafana (dashboard id: 74b-consume) showing sample of 12 customers where backfill creates +1.5–6% step changes when async enrichment arrives. Logged customer impact and prioritized as P1.

2026-01-18 @Marco Liu: Spike root cause narrowed to two mechanisms: (1) events from async-enrich pipeline lack stable idempotency keys causing duplicate ingestion when streaming replay happens, (2) console aggregation uses ingestion_time bucketing which interacts badly with shard-replay ordering. Experiment plan drafted.

2026-01-22 @Marco Liu: Ran PoC that attaches deterministic idempotency keys (source:event_uuid) and switched aggregator to canonical_event_time with jitter-corrected shard offsets. Preliminary results: duplicates dropped ~60% on test shard but introduced small reordering artifacts at window edges.

2026-01-29 @PM - Sienna Gomez: PM review — prefer approach that trades a short finalization delay for consistent charts. Approved stabilization window of 48 hours and requirement for Console to show 'as-of' timestamps so customers understand ongoing adjustments.

2026-01-31 @Design - Priya Nair: UX review — added mockups for per-model chart toggle (As-of / Finalized) and an inline microcopy explaining 'finalized' meaning and reconciliation timestamps. Provided feedback to emphasize audit links to original events.

2026-02-02 @Marco Liu: Integration branch opened: github.com/redwood-inference/metrics/compare/ENG-206784-canonical-meter (PR 5123). Implementation includes: idempotency layer in ingress, a retention-aware exponential decay smoother with 48h horizon, and reconciliation job that emits finalized deltas to the metrics store. Running integration test against 200k synthetic events.

2026-02-03 @SRE - Elena Kovac: Observability checklist added. New metric 'reconciler.finalized_lag_seconds' instrumented and alert playbook drafted for >72h lag. Load test shows reconciliation job completes within 32m for worst-case 48h window on staging cluster.

2026-02-03 @Marco Liu: Note — trade-offs documented: choosing canonical_event_time (event_emitted_at) reduces cross-shard skew but requires careful correction for clock-drift; added server-side watermarking and per-shard clock-offset correction step. Clock-offset correction validated in staging with <10ms residuals.

2026-02-03 @Aisha Patel: Next steps — finish PR code review, run org-wide A/B test on 10% of traffic for 2 weeks, update Console to show 'finalized' series and audit links, and schedule post-deploy runbook review with support and billing teams.
